candidates.statement: A fully-extended n-dimensional topological field theory is a sym- metric monoidal functor of (∞, n)-categories Z : Bordn →C. The (∞, n) category Bordn has objects 0-dimensional manifolds, 1-morphisms are cobordisms between 0-dimensional manifolds, 2-morphisms are cobordisms between cobordisms, etc. The n-morphisms can be interpreted as an n-dimensional manifold with corners. The (n + 1)-morphisms are diffeomorphisms between two n-manifold with corners, and the (n + 2)-morphisms are isotopies between diffeomorphisms, etc. This construction was proposed by [Lur08] and later corrected by [CS19] and appeared as the thesis of [Sch14]. candidates.statement: The 2-dimensional oriented bordism category Cob(2) is the free sym- metric monoidal category with a single commutative Frobenius algebra object. In par- ticular the category of oriented 2-dimensional topological field theories is equivalent to the category of commutative Frobenius algebras. This theorem was widely known and formal proofs appeared in numerous papers such as [Dij89], [Abr96], and J. [Koc03]. candidates.statement: 1.2. (Binary Relation) Let C be a category and a, b ∈obj(C). A bi- nary relation Ra,b on HomC(a, b) is a subset Ra,b ⊂HomC(a, b) × HomC(a, b). We write fRa,bg if (f, g) ∈Ra,b. We say R is a binary relation on homs of C if R = {Ra,b | a, b ∈obj(C)} is a collection of binary relations on all pairs of objects of C. If a pair of morphisms (f, f′) is in Ra,b, we write fRa,bf′, or f = f′ if the context is clear.

Moreover, H factors uniquely through the quotient: H = H ◦Q where Q : C →C/ ≡H and H : C/ ≡H→D where H(a) = H(a) and H([f]) = H(f).

candidates.statement: 1.6. (Quotient Category) Let C be a category and R a congruence on C. Then the quotient category C/R has the same objects as C and the morphisms HomC/R(a, b) = HomC(a, b)/Ra,b are those of C modulo the equivalence relation Ra,b. If R is a binary relation, the quotient category C/R is defined as C/R′ where R′ is the least congruence containing R.

2.1. ((∞, 1)-category) An (∞, 1)-category is a complete Segal space X•. That is, a simplicial object in topological spaces satisfying completeness and the Segal condition. See [Lur08] for details about completeness and Segal condition. See [Zha13, section 2] for a comparison between the different settings of complete Segal spaces. Here we specialize to the setting of topological spaces and retreat to compactly generated Hausdorff spaces or CW spaces if pathologies arise.
